sample_unit: clinician raters evaluating 30 synthetic discharge letter summaries

links.outcome: Hallucinations and omissions in LLM discharge letter summaries, by section
links.effect: Content positive response rate 78%; medication section lowest with highest hallucination rate; missing information most common error across all sections.
links.quote: The positive response rate for content was overall moderate (78%), with the best performance observed in the medical history section and the lowest performance observed in the medication section, which also showed the highest rate of hallucinations and the weakest interrater consensus.

links.outcome: Accuracy of medication details in LLM-generated summaries
links.effect: Medication section had lowest content performance, highest hallucination rate and weakest consensus; identified as key vulnerability.
links.quote: Semantic integrity, especially regarding medication details, was identified as a key vulnerability.

unlisted_practices: Expert-cocreated evaluation framework with binary layout and content items plus global rating for LLM summaries

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the performance, accuracy, errors (omissions/hallucinations), and inter-rater reliability of clinician evaluations on GPT-4o-generated discharge summaries using synthetic letters.
